newsitem.title: POLAND: Gdansk yard applies for loan to WBK.
newsitem.headline: Gdansk yard applies for loan to WBK.

text.p: Poland's bankrupt Gdansk shipyard has applied to Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy SA (WBK) for a loan to finance the construction of a ship for a German shipowner, the bank and the yard said on Tuesday.
"Talks continue with WBK on financing the construction of the first ship for Schoeller," the shipyard's deputy receiver Wieslaw Szaj told Reuters.
The bank confirmed in a statement it had received a loan application from the yard but said that after reviewing the project it had decided that the loan would require full government guarantees.

"The analysis conducted by WBK shows that because of the risks involved in financing this project, extending a loan would be possible only on the condition of securing 100-percent state treasury guarantees," the bank said.

Schoeller Holding Ltd, based in Cyprus, wants to order five ships from the Gdansk shipyard, worth $27.5 million each, but the company, burdened with a 415 million zloty debt, needs to secure financing for the contract.

Szaj said that the state-owned Pekao SA bank was likely to extend another loan, worth $16 million, which would enable the shipyard to hire 800 workers to finish the construction of a vessel for a foreign contractor.
"There are substantial chances that the loan will be granted. The bank should take the decision on the loan on Thursday," Szaj said.

Szaj also said that should WBK refuse the loan the shipyard would start financing the construction from proceeds from the ongoing sale of contribution coupons, launched last month to save the firm. The sale has so far brought 17 million zlotys.
Polish artists and singers are scheduled to hold a concert in Warsaw late on Tuesday to raise funds for the shipyard.
The shipyard, the cradle of the Solidarity trade union, went bankrupt last year and its receiver started dismissing its last 3,800 workers last month.
The receiver and the government are looking for a strategic investor to save the yard.
